title: API context enrichment and observability contract
author: Ava Mendes
content:
Summary

This document defines the contract for API-level context enrichment and how services in Redwood Inference must propagate, attach, and emit telemetry context. The goal is to standardize fields that are required for reliable tracing, request attribution, cost allocation, and quality monitoring while constraining telemetry cardinality and preserving backward compatibility.

Why this matters

- Improves cross-service observability for SLO debugging and post-incident triage.
- Ensures consistent cost and customer attribution across the edge, gateway, and runtime.
- Prevents high-cardinality telemetry explosion by restricting optional enrichment and providing cardinality budgets.

Scope and applicability

This contract applies to public REST/HTTP and internal gRPC endpoints served by: edge-proxy, inference-gateway, request-router, runtime-manager, dedicated-allocator, and private-sidecar. It applies to:
- Synchronous request paths (text/generation/embeddings)
- Streaming endpoints (server streaming + chunked HTTP)
- Background async workers that handle user-attributable requests (batch rerank, offline embedding jobs)

It does NOT apply to:
- Internal health-check endpoints (/healthz)
- Admin-only control plane RPCs (unless marked as customer-facing)

Core principles

1. Minimal required context: every customer-facing request MUST carry the minimum context fields (see "Required headers").
2. Low-entropy defaults: fields with potentially high cardinality must be represented by tiered keys and capped enumerations.
3. Observable fallbacks: services must emit an explicit metric when required context is missing, with SLO for remediation.
4. Backwards compatible enrichment: new optional fields can be introduced only behind feature flags and with rollout validation.

Contract: Required headers and metadata

Table: canonical request-level fields (all transmitted as HTTP headers or equivalent gRPC metadata)

- X-Request-Id: string (uuid4 recommended). Purpose: global request correlation. Required.
- X-Customer-Id: string (tenant id). Purpose: billing & attribution. Required for authenticated requests.
- X-Route-Profile: enum {low_latency, standard, bulk}. Purpose: routing & SLO bucketing. Required for any inference endpoint.
- X-Auth-Mode: enum {api_key, oauth, mTLS}. Purpose: policy decisions and audit. Required.
- X-Attribution-Source: enum {ui, api, worker, webhook}. Purpose: product-level attribution. Required where applicable; set to "api" if unknown.

Optional but restricted enrichment (must be approved)

- X-User-Session: opaque string (session id). Use only when session-level routing is necessary. Cardinality budget: max 100k active session identifiers emitted as tag per hour per service.
- X-Experiment-Id: string (A/B test id). Allowed for test cohorts; must be short. Cardinality budget: 50 distinct experiment ids per service.
- X-Prompt-Variant: short token (<=24 chars). Use sparingly — count toward high-cardinality metrics and traces.

Trace propagation and spans

- Use W3C trace-context (traceparent, tracestate) as primary propagation mechanism.
- Services must not drop existing traceparent headers; when starting new traces, origin must be set to 'edge-proxy' or 'runtime' as appropriate.
- When converting from legacy proprietary tracing (X-B3-*), the gateway must translate to W3C headers and emit a conversion metric: telemetry.trace.legacy_conversion_count.

Telemetry emission rules (metrics, logs, traces)

- Metrics:
  - Emit request_latency_ms as histogram with buckets: 1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 500, 2000, 10000 ms. Tag dimensions: service_name, route_profile, customer_tier (free/paid/enterprise), failure_type.
  - Cardinality cap: no service should emit metrics with more than 25k unique tag value combinations per hour. Services exceeding this cap must emit a telemetry.alert with severity=warning.

- Traces & spans:
  - Sampling: default 0.5% for user-requests; 100% for errors (status >=500) and for requests flagged with route_profile=low_latency.
  - Span naming: service.operation[.subop], e.g., inference-gateway.request.validate, runtime-manager.kv-prefetch.

- Logs: structured JSON. Required base fields: timestamp, service_name, env, level, request_id, trace_id (if available), customer_id (if available).

Schema examples

1) Minimal HTTP request headers (single-line example):

curl -H "X-Request-Id: 7f3e1a9b-2c6a-4a4b-9d05-1f8b2f6d8c3a" \n     -H "X-Customer-Id: cust_42" \n     -H "X-Route-Profile: low_latency" \n     -H "traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01" \n     https://inference.example.com/v1/generate

2) Example JSON envelope for telemetry-relevant request metadata (internal transport):

{
  "request_id": "7f3e1a9b-2c6a-4a4b-9d05-1f8b2f6d8c3a",
  "customer_id": "cust_42",
  "route_profile": "low_latency",
  "origin": "edge-proxy"
}

Backward compatibility and rollouts

- New header fields MUST be introduced behind a boolean feature flag that is recognized by the gateway and runtime.
- A compatibility test harness (api-context-lint) will run in CI for all services. It validates: presence of required headers, valid enum values for X-Route-Profile and X-Auth-Mode, and cardinality checks on enrichment fields.
- Rollout phases:
  1. Design & doc (this page).
  2. Canary injection at edge-proxy (5% of traffic, run for 72 hours).
  3. Server-side enforcement in staging with api-context-lint.
  4. Gradual increase to 25%, 50%, 100% with monitoring alarms.
  5. Post-rollout audit (7/30/90 day checks) and potential reversion plan.

Enforcement and validation tooling

- api-context-lint: command-line tool invoked by CI. Rules: header_presence, enum_validation, cardinality_estimate.
- runtime-gateway-plugin: lightweight middleware that can inject defaults (e.g., X-Attribution-Source: api) and emit telemetry.missing_context_count metric.
- telemetry-proxy: central sidecar service that validates and enriches tracecontext for private deployments; it can be configured to reject requests missing required headers if the customer opts into strict-mode.

SLOs and alerting

- Required header availability: 99.95% of incoming authenticated requests must contain X-Customer-Id and X-Request-Id. Alert: telemetry.missing_required_headers_rate > 0.05% sustained for 10 minutes.
- Trace conversion: legacy-to-w3c conversion success >= 99.9% (metric: telemetry.trace.legacy_conversion_success).
- Metric cardinality cap: enforced as a soft SLO with warning at 90% of 25k unique tag combos/hour and hard alarm at 100%.

Ownership and responsibilities

- API Design/Ownership: api-platform team (primary contact: Priya Rao). Responsible for header enums, feature-flagging, and api-context-lint rules.
- Observability: infra-observability team (primary contact: Michael Chen). Responsible for ingestion, sampling config, and cardinality monitoring.
- Runtime & Gateway: serving-runtime team (primary contact: Diego Alvarez). Responsible for middleware, translation logic, and runtime enforcement.

Operational runbook (summary)

1. If telemetry.missing_required_headers_rate fires:
   a. Notify owning service on-call.
   b. Confirm client upgrade or gateway regression.
   c. If >5% of traffic missing: apply emergency gateway defaults and open a P0 incident.
2. If cardinality alarms fire:
   a. Identify top offending tag by service and metric.
   b. Roll back recently-introduced enrichment fields or gate them behind a flag.

Appendix: header reference table

- X-Request-Id: uuid4, required, immutable.
- X-Customer-Id: short tenant id (alphanumeric), required for authenticated requests.
- X-Route-Profile: {low_latency, standard, bulk}, required.
- X-Auth-Mode: {api_key, oauth, mTLS}, required.
- X-Attribution-Source: {ui, api, worker, webhook}, default 'api'.
- X-Experiment-Id: optional, admin-approved, maximum 50 distinct ids.
